title: THE PROMISE WE COULD NOT KEEP

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'or if anyone thoughtlessly takes an oath to do anything, whether good or evil (in any matter one might carelessly swear about) even though they are unaware of it, but then they learn of it and realise their guilt.'" - Lev 5:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A rash promise. Words spoken quickly, without thinking — and then the person realises what they have committed themselves to.

The Bible has several sad examples of this. Jephthah made a reckless vow and lived with its consequences (Judg 11:30-35). Herod promised a dancing girl anything she asked and had John the Baptist executed rather than lose face (Mk 6:23-26). Peter swore he would never deny Jesus, and did so three times before dawn (Mtt 26:35, 69-75).

Words are not cheap. God takes them seriously even when we do not.

Jesus addressed this directly. He told His followers not to swear elaborate oaths at all, but simply: let your "Yes" be "Yes," and your "No," "No" (Mtt 5:37). The point is that a person of integrity does not need to reinforce their word with dramatic guarantees. Their ordinary speech is reliable.

Most of us have made promises we could not keep — to a child, a spouse, a friend, or to God Himself. Perhaps in a difficult moment we told God we would change something, and we did not.

God's provision here is not condemnation. It is a way back for the person who spoke too quickly. Confess it honestly, and where possible, make it right.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there a promise I have made and quietly let go of?
2. Do people find my ordinary word reliable, or do I need to dress it up?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, forgive me for words spoken carelessly and promises I did not keep. Make my speech simple and true. Amen.
